les: Geboue met 'n werk om te doen
kaps_punt: Geboue in verskillende plekke en hul gebruike - geboue soos huise, diereskuilings, winkels, skole, klinieke, banke, kantore, plekke van aanbidding, fabrieke, motorhuise en treinstasies

items.bewering: Mense het elkeen van hierdie geboue ontwerp en gebou om 'n bepaalde werk te doen. Daardie werk gee vir mense iets wat hulle nodig het of gebruik.
items.blok: Mense bou vir 'n rede
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Building' (en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Building): buildings serve needs such as shelter, security, living space and storage, and are shaped by specific uses. Municipal and legal definitions describe a building as a structure designed or occupied for shelter or for a use. A building later put to another use was still built for a purpose, so the claim holds.

items.bewering: Sommige van hierdie geboue voorsien in 'n behoefte van die mense daar. 'n Behoefte is iets wat mense nodig het om veilig en gesond te leef.
items.blok: Mense bou vir 'n rede
items.bron: The standard needs/wants distinction in introductory economics defines a need as something necessary for survival, such as food, water, clothing and shelter. If needs go unmet the result may be illness or death (Nagwa, 'Basic Economic Concepts'; Wikipedia, 'Want'). 'Veilig en gesond leef' is a fair Grade 4 wording of that. No online Afrikaans dictionary entry (WAT/HAT) for 'behoefte' could be reached. The everyday Afrikaans and Dutch word is broader and also covers desire, but as the lesson's teaching definition it is accurate.

items.bewering: Huise en woonstelle voorsien in die behoefte aan skuiling.
items.blok: Huise gee skuiling
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'shelter' (per search result): 'the fact of having a place to live or stay, considered as a basic human need'. Food, clothing and shelter are the classic basic needs in the needs/wants literature.

items.bewering: Skuiling is 'n plek wat mense of diere veilig hou en teen wind, reën, koue en hitte beskerm.
items.blok: Huise gee skuiling
items.bron: American Heritage Dictionary via Wordnik: shelter is 'something, especially a structure, that provides cover or protection, as from the weather'. Oxford Learner's: protection from rain, danger or attack. Britannica Learner's: 'covered and protected from danger, bad weather'.

items.bewering: Op 'n plaas bou mense ook 'n stal of 'n hok wat die diere teen reën en koue beskerm.
items.blok: Huise gee skuiling
items.bron: University of New Hampshire Cooperative Extension animal-shelter rubric (Vermont Legislature, H.254 testimony) and USDA National Agroforestry Center: livestock shelters exist mainly to keep wind and wet off the animals. A stable is where horses are housed and protects them from rain, wind and sun. The 'wat' clause is restrictive (a stall or pen that protects them), so it does not claim that every hok is roofed. Some local pens, such as an open skaaphok, are not.

items.bewering: Winkel: mense koop hier kos, klere en ander goed wat hulle nodig het.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Merriam-Webster, 'shop': a building or room stocked with items for sale, where goods are sold retail.

items.bewering: Skool: kinders leer hier lees en skryf en baie ander dinge.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'school': a place where children go to be educated. Wikipedia, 'School': an institution and building designed to provide learning environments for the teaching of students under teachers.

items.bewering: Kliniek: 'n verpleegster of 'n dokter help siek mense en gee inentings.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: GCIS South Africa Yearbook 2009, ch. 12 (Health): primary health care services at clinics include immunisation, treatment of disease, maternity and child care. Gauteng Health MEC, Dec 2024 (IOL): 'Immunisation is free at all public clinics and community healthcare centres'. KZN study (NISC African Journal of Primary Health Care) and SA Family Practice papers: SA clinics are largely run by registered nurses, and doctors visit. 'Verpleegster of dokter' is therefore accurate, with the nurse correctly named first.

items.bewering: Bank: mense hou hulle geld hier veilig en kan dit weer gaan haal.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Sowetan Live, 13 Dec 2012, quoting Standard Bank's head of inclusive banking: depositing cash in a bank account is one of the best ways to keep it safe, and deposits and withdrawals can be made at bank outlets. SARB statement, Aug 2025 (IOL): deposits at licensed banks are protected by the Corporation for Deposit Insurance (CODI). Mapping checked: the wording could suggest that the bank keeps a person's own notes in the building, which is not how banks work. A Grade 4 learner would not plausibly reason further from it into an error, and the stated function (money kept safe and withdrawable) is true.

items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'office': a room, set of rooms or building where people work, usually sitting at desks. Wordup dictionary: staff work at desks with computers, phones and printers.

items.bewering: Plek van aanbidding: mense kom hier bymekaar om saam te aanbid.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Place of worship': a specially designed structure or space where individuals or a group such as a congregation come to perform acts of devotion. Vocabulary.com: any building where congregations gather for prayer.

items.bewering: Fabriek: 'n gebou waar mense of masjiene baie van dieselfde produk maak om te verkoop. (Also the begrip entry 'fabriek', word for word.)
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk; begrip: fabriek
items.bron: Oxford Learner's Dictionaries, 'factory' (per search result): a building or group of buildings where goods are made, mainly by machine. Merriam-Webster Learner's: a building or group of buildings where products are made. Britannica, 'factory system': production concentrated in specialised establishments built around machinery, the basis of mass production of standardised goods. 'Baie van dieselfde produk' describes mass production. That is the typical case, not every factory, but it is a fair Grade 4 simplification and not a falsehood.

items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Garage': a covered structure built for parking, storing and protecting vehicles. Oxford Learner's: a building for keeping one or more cars in.

items.bewering: Treinstasie: treine stop hier sodat mense kan opklim en afklim.
items.blok: Elke gebou het sy eie werk
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Train station': a railway facility where trains stop to load or unload passengers, freight or both. Wiktionary: a place where trains stop so passengers can board and leave.

items.bewering: Nie elke plek het al hierdie geboue nie. Op 'n plaas is daar gewoonlik nie 'n treinstasie nie.
items.blok: Nie elke plek het alles nie
items.bron: Parliamentary reply NW325/NW3194 to the Minister of Transport (pmg.org.za): PRASA's main-line passenger stations are named after towns (Acornhoek, Hoedspruit, Zeerust, Vryburg). Metrorail's 468 stations are mostly metropolitan. Freight sidings exist on some rural land but are not passenger stations. 'Gewoonlik' carries the qualifier the claim needs.

items.bewering: Twee skole in twee dorpe doen dieselfde werk en lyk tog meestal verskillend.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Mail & Guardian, 2005 (Veerle Dieltiens, on school architecture, quoting Helene Nienaber, chief architect of the Gauteng Department of Education): after 1994 Gauteng inherited the former Department of Education and Training's school-building rule book and built schools from those standard plans for about three years, with a standard 7 m x 8 m classroom. University of Pretoria thesis 'The provision of schools by the DET in South Africa during 1983-1994' (repository.up.ac.za/handle/2263/76383): the DET introduced standardised classroom plans and modular grids for its school building. M&G 2015: Gauteng's newer schools were built to a prototype. Many South African schools were therefore deliberately built to the same plans. 'Meestal verskillend' is a generalisation that no source supports, and a learner whose own and neighbouring schools follow one standard plan will see it fail in front of them. The quantifier is the fault, not the idea.
items.regstelling: Narrow the quantifier and leave the subject as it is: two schools with the same job do not always look the same, and can look different in two places. This is what the block's own heading ('nie altyd eenders nie') and its closing sentence ('kan dus in twee plekke anders lyk') already say, so the opening sentence should match them rather than claim 'meestal'. Do not add a sentence about standard plans; narrowing is enough.

items.bewering: Die werk binne die gebou help bepaal sy grootte en sy vorm.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Wikipedia, 'Building': building form has been shaped by specific uses, available materials, weather, land and ground conditions. 'Help bepaal' correctly makes function one factor among several.

items.bewering: Die klimaat van die plek speel ook 'n rol. Geboue in 'n streek met baie reën kry dikwels steiler dakke.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Austrian Open-Air Museum Stübing (Universalmuseum Joanneum), roof landscapes page: steep roofs tended to be found in areas of high precipitation, and flat roofs were sufficient in dry climates. BRANZ (NZ building research), 'Resilient roof design and construction': steeper pitches shed water faster. South African contrast: Karoo brakdak flat roofs in arid country (Koedoe 66(2), 2024; Fagan, 'Brakdak: Flatroofs in the Karoo', 2008). 'Dikwels' is the right strength, because materials and culture also shape roofs.

items.bewering: Mense bou ook met materiaal soos klip of klei wat naby hulle lê.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Heritage Portal, 'Variation and change in the architecture of early farm dwellings around Pretoria': early farm buildings relied on nearby clay, earth and stone. Franco Frescura, SA History Online, indigenous architecture: rural southern African dwellings built predominantly of saplings, timber, clay, grass and dung, with stone rubble and shale in some regions. University of the Free State paper on earth construction as an African tradition.

items.bewering: Die gebou se grootte hang ook af van hoeveel mense dit gebruik. 'n Skool vir duisend kinders het meer klaskamers as 'n klein plaasskool.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Mail & Guardian, 'Glimpse into a different world' (2009) and Sowetan, 'The school with 13 pupils and a teacher' (2014): South African farm schools are small, with one to three teachers and several grades per classroom (multigrade). M&G 2015: Gauteng 'smart school' mega schools for up to 1 200 pupils. A school of a thousand learners is realistic, and it needs far more classrooms than a small farm school.

items.bewering: Hierdie dinge werk saam wanneer mense 'n gebou beplan. Twee geboue met dieselfde werk kan dus in twee plekke anders lyk.
items.blok: Hoekom lyk twee skole nie altyd eenders nie?
items.bron: Follows from the confirmed factors above (use, climate, local materials, number of users; Wikipedia, 'Building'). 'Kan' is the correct strength. This sentence is the careful form the block's opening sentence should match (see the 'meestal' item).

items.bewering: Begrip 'behoefte': Iets wat mense nodig het om veilig en gesond te leef.
items.blok: begrip: behoefte
items.bron: As for the study-text definition: needs are what is necessary for survival and wellbeing (Nagwa, 'Basic Economic Concepts'; Wikipedia, 'Want'). The entry is true read on its own.

items.bewering: Begrip 'skuiling': 'n Plek wat mense of diere veilig hou en teen wind, reën, koue en hitte beskerm.
items.blok: begrip: skuiling
items.bron: American Heritage Dictionary via Wordnik, Oxford Learner's and Britannica Learner's, 'shelter': a structure giving protection from weather and danger. The entry is true read on its own.

opsomming: One claim must be narrowed: the opening sentence says two schools in two towns 'meestal' look different, but many South African schools were deliberately built to the same standard plans, so it should say what the block's own heading and closing sentence say (they do not always look alike, and can look different). Everything else was confirmed, and the lesson has no superlatives and no comparisons beyond the bank wording, whose mapping holds at Grade 4.
